name: FFmpeg GEQ Procedural Alpha Masks
use_when: The agent needs a programmatic grayscale mask such as a linear wipe, radial reveal, Gaussian spotlight, checker debug mask, or wave shimmer.
A mask should be generated from resolution, position, and time rather than drawn by hand.
The mask recipe should be reproducible outside CapCut.
avoid_when: The mask shape is easier to express with Remotion CSS/SVG masks.
The expression is slow and will be reused without pre-rendering.
The effect is applied to dense captions where wave or texture reduces readability.
The mask has not been previewed independently.

timeline_pattern.preview_rule: Render the mask alone before compositing.
timeline_pattern.performance_rule: Pre-render expensive or reused masks instead of recalculating them inside every final graph.

motion.rule: Use X/Y/W/H expressions for spatial shape and time offsets for movement; keep text masks subtle enough to preserve reading.

keyframe_values.linear_mask: Drive visibility from X or Y for left/right or top/bottom reveals.
keyframe_values.radial_mask: Drive visibility from distance to a center point for spotlight or aura reveals.
keyframe_values.wave_mask: Use sine motion only for stylized shimmer or liquid effects and keep duration short.

sound.rule: Wave, shimmer, or scan masks may use one soft matching cue, but only if it lands on visible motion and stays below speech.

captions.rule: Do not use wave or checker procedural masks on accessibility captions; reserve them for short emphasis or title graphics.

color.rule: Gray mask values create partial transparency, so check glow/blur edges over both light and dark backgrounds.

implementation.ffmpeg: Generate grayscale masks with geq expressions, preview or pre-render them, then attach with alphamerge to the foreground stream.
implementation.remotion: Equivalent masks can often be implemented with CSS gradients, SVG masks, or frame-driven canvas/SVG values.
implementation.blender: Use procedural textures, gradients, or compositor math nodes as matte sources.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Approximate with Split/Film Strip masks, feathered masks, or imported pre-rendered mask overlays where supported.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use track mattes, gradient wipes, radial masks, or imported pre-rendered matte clips.

common_mistakes: Using a one-pixel checker or aggressive wave that looks like compression dirt.
Leaving a heavy geq expression in every render pass when a pre-rendered mask would be safer.
Forgetting to normalize by frame dimensions and breaking different aspect ratios.
Using partial gray mask tails that leave text semi-transparent after the reveal should be complete.
qc: Mask preview direction, polarity, and softness are correct.
Mask expression works at the final resolution and aspect ratio.
Heavy masks are pre-rendered when reused.
Wave/liquid masks do not reduce text readability.
The final reveal has no lingering semi-transparent sliver.
